pairs: Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum, et comedat fructum pomorum suorum. Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa; messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis; comedi favum cum melle meo; bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo; comedite, amici, et bibite, et inebriamini, carissimi.
Bride: May my beloved enter into his garden, and eat the fruit of his apple trees.
I have arrived in my garden,
I have eaten the honeycomb with my honey.
quia caput meum plenum est rore,
I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends,
and drink, and be inebriated, O most beloved.
The voice of my beloved knocking:
Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen, et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus.
Groom to Bride: Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my immaculate one. For my head is full of dew, and the locks of my hair are full of the drops of the night.
Bride: I have taken off my tunic;
how shall I be clothed in it?
et digiti mei pleni myrrha probatissima.
I have washed my feet; how shall I spoil them?
Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo, at ille declinaverat, atque transierat. Anima mea liquefacta est, ut locutus est; quæsivi, et non inveni illum; vocavi, et non respondit mihi.
My beloved put his hand through the window, and my inner self was moved by his touch.
Invenerunt me custodes qui circumeunt civitatem;
I rose up in order to open to my beloved.
Tulerunt pallium meum mihi custodes murorum.
and my fingers were full of the finest myrrh.
Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, si inveneritis dilectum meum, ut nuntietis ei quia amore langueo.
I opened the bolt of my door to my beloved. But he had turned aside and had gone away. My soul melted when he spoke. I sought him, and did not find him. I called, and he did not answer me.
Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto,
The keepers who circulate through the city found me.
qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto,
The keepers of the walls took my veil away from me.
I bind you by oath, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved,
announce to him that I languish through love.
Chorus to Bride: What kind of beloved is your beloved,
O most beautiful among women? What kind of beloved is your beloved,
so that you would bind us by oath?
Oculi ejus sicut columbæ super rivulos aquarum,
My beloved is white and ruddy,
His head is like the finest gold.
consitæ a pigmentariis. Labia ejus lilia,
His locks are like the heights of palm trees,
and as black as a raven.
aureæ, plenæ hyacinthis. Venter ejus eburneus,
which have been washed with milk over rivulets of waters,
and which reside near plentiful streams.
Crura illius columnæ marmoreæ quæ fundatæ sunt super bases aureas.
His cheeks are like a courtyard of aromatic plants, sown by perfumers.
et ipse est amicus meus, filiæ Jerusalem.
Quo abiit dilectus tuus, o pulcherrima mulierum? quo declinavit dilectus tuus? et quæremus eum tecum.

His legs are columns of marble, which have been established over bases of gold. His appearance is like that of Lebanon, elect like the cedars. His throat is most sweet, and he is entirely desirable. Such is my beloved, and he is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem. Chorus to Bride: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? To where has your beloved turned aside, so that we may seek him with you?
